text: Gordon had nine points in 27 minutes as a starter. The show said his usage rate has dropped and he has fallen off this season.
Aaron Gordon played just 24 minutes in Denver's loss, and the show is comfortable moving on from him.
Aaron Nesmith played 33 minutes as a starter on November 13. The show said he stays worth rostering until Tyrese Haliburton returns.
The show said Aaron Nesmith has a secure starting role and can play 34 minutes, though some nights he plays closer to 28. He started and played 33 and 36 minutes in his last two games.
Nesmith scored two points on 14 percent shooting in 29 minutes. The show said he really struggles with Tyrese Haliburton out and is hard to trust right now.

Atlanta started Wiggins on 11/18 with Kingston Flemings out, and he played 26 minutes while RayJ Dennis played only 10 off the bench. Nickeil Alexander-Walker played 32 minutes in that game, and the show called that a role he should keep.
Aaron Wiggins started again on Friday, Nov. 20, and played 34 minutes with Kingston Flemings (back) and CJ McCollum (calf) both out. It was his second straight start in place of the injured guards.

Bailey was held to 8 shots on Nov. 17, and his minutes fell to 23 after he played 29 to 35 minutes in his prior games. The show said he should stay rostered while Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen are out for another two or three weeks. Bailey bounced back to 27 minutes and 19 points on Nov. 18.
Dan Besbris listed Ace Bailey as a top-100 season-long pickup because Jaren Jackson Jr. is out, which opens up minutes for him. Bailey played 27 minutes in his last game on 11/18.
Ace Bailey started but played only 24 minutes on 11/20, his second game under 25 minutes in his last four. The show said it is not dropping him but that he is starting to frustrate.
Mara moved back into the starting lineup and Kenrich Williams went to the bench. Mara played 27 minutes with eight assists, and the show said to keep rolling with him.
Aday Mara started and played 29 minutes on Friday, Nov. 20. Oklahoma City is 8-5 since losing three starters to long-term injuries, and Mara has been a starter in that stretch.
The show said Adem Bona will be out for Saturday's game against Milwaukee. He is listed with a cervical spine sprain and has not played in the 76ers' recent games.

The show said AJ Dybantsa is a tough play at $6,600 because he shares the scoring load with Kyshawn George, Anthony Davis and Trae Young. Dybantsa had 13 points and 23.5 DK points in 34 minutes on Nov 11.

AJ Dybantsa scored 12.2 of his 28.2 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 28-point loss against HOU on Sunday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.
AJ Dybantsa scored 16 points on 18 shots with a high usage rate. The show said his production has been middling and his shooting has been poor.

AJ Dybantsa has started every game and played 30 to 44 minutes over his last eight games. The show said he is off his minutes limit and should play close to 40 minutes against Memphis, and it preferred him to Kyshawn George.

Dybantsa played 38 minutes and posted 23 points and 12 rebounds on 11/18 while making no threes. The show said he scores by getting to the rim and likes his 11/20 matchup against a Chicago team that it says allows the most paint points in the league.
AJ Dybantsa posted back-to-back double-doubles on 11/18 and 11/20 while playing 37 or more minutes in both games. The show said he is looking better and more comfortable.

Ajay Mitchell is questionable with a left ankle sprain, and Oklahoma City is still without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams at the Clippers. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has scored 26 to 31 points in each of his last four games.
Ajay Mitchell returned from a sprained ankle on November 15 after missing the November 13 game, and he started and played 27 minutes. The show called him a full start going forward.
Ajay Mitchell kept his starting job and played 31 minutes, though his production has slowed lately. The show said the job is his and he should be held.
Al Horford sat Monday, Nov. 2, for rest on the second night of a back-to-back, not an injury, and is available Thursday.

Al Horford started over Will Richard, but he went scoreless in 14 minutes and came off the bench in the second half. Charles Bassey started the second half instead, and the show said Steve Kerr will keep mixing lineups.

Horford has started two of Golden State's last five games but has played only 13, 15, 21, 10 and 14 minutes in that span, including 14 minutes in his start on 11/16. The show said his minimum $3,500 price is the only thing making him a value, and it said it would rather see Charles Bassey or De'Anthony Melton start.

Horford came off the bench for 17 minutes on 11/19 after missing 11/18, and he has played 10 to 21 minutes in each recent game. The show said he simply cannot play big minutes at his age, which is why Charles Bassey has taken the center job.

Caruso returned on Nov. 4 after missing four games and played 20 minutes off the bench with seven points. The show said he should carve out his own role with Cason Wallace and Jalen Williams likely out for the season and Chet Holmgren sidelined.

Alex Caruso moved into the starting lineup with Ajay Mitchell out and played 29 minutes on a back-to-back for 14 points, seven rebounds, three steals, and four threes. Kenrich Williams went to the bench. The show said Ajay Mitchell's ankle injury may not be significant, and Mitchell and Jalen Williams will cut into Caruso's role when they return.

The show listed Alex Caruso as a short-term pickup while Ajay Mitchell is out. With Mitchell sidelined by a right ankle sprain, Caruso started on November 11 and played 29 minutes, then came off the bench for 27 minutes on November 13 when Kenrich Williams started.

Caruso started on Nov 11 and played 29 minutes, then came off the bench for 27 and 18 minutes in his next two games. The show said a lot of guard minutes are up for grabs in Oklahoma City, so it would hold him through a bad game.

Alex Caruso left the November 18 game with right hip soreness after only 9 minutes, and he was ruled out again on November 20. The show said these short injuries seem to hit him every four or five games.
Alex Caruso played only 9 minutes because he could not finish the game. The show said his inability to last through games is the main problem with trusting him.
Alex Karaban played 29 minutes and went scoreless while Sacramento was without Zach LaVine and De'Andre Hunter. The show called him the worst pick in his draft class.
Alex Morales, a two-way player, made his first NBA start after Jamal Cain was injured. He played 18 minutes and scored five points. Jase Richardson stayed on the bench for 20 minutes.
He is questionable with left knee soreness, and Deandre Ayton started at center in his place Monday and played 24 minutes.

Alex Sarr played 27 minutes on November 15 with the rest of Washington's starting lineup intact. The show said 27 minutes is the expected number for him and that he has come around after a slow start.
Alex Sarr scored 25 points with three blocks after scoring 30 points in his previous game. The show said his usage has gone up after a poor start, though his shooting will not stay this hot.
Alex Sarr (illness) and Tre Johnson (low back soreness) are questionable against Houston, which would open minutes for Bilal Coulibaly.

Alex Sarr had a poor line but still played 31 minutes as Washington lost its eighth straight game. The show said his overall activity has been trending up and that the playing time is the part to trust.
Alex Sarr played just 22 minutes but still posted a useful line. The show said his minutes have been all over the place this season.

Alex Sarr started but played only 20 minutes and had 10.25 DraftKings points. His minutes have dropped in each of his last four games, from 44 to 27, 31, 22 and now 20, and the show called his season very streaky.
Graves played 31 minutes off the bench with Barrett and Barnes out, which was far more than his usual 13 to 18 minutes. The show liked seeing the team trust him but is not adding him.

Allen Graves moved into the starting lineup on Friday, Nov. 20, with Collin Murray-Boyles in the concussion protocol and RJ Barrett out with a hamstring strain, and he played 33 minutes, well above his recent bench role.
He missed Friday with low back soreness, and Clint Capela started at center with 11 rebounds and five assists in 30 minutes. Houston has not posted its injury report for Saturday yet.

The show said Alperen Sengun has an easy matchup on Nov 13 because Utah is without Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic, leaving Mo Bamba and Jaxson Hayes to guard him. Houston's own centers Clint Capela and Steven Adams are still out.

Houston is without Clint Capela and Steven Adams, and Marcus Smart is serving a league suspension. Alperen Sengun has played 35 to 39 minutes in three of his last four games, but Houston is a 17.5-point favorite over a Utah team missing Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr.

Alperen Sengun played 28 minutes in a 28-point win against WAS on Sunday, 8 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 45.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Alperen Sengun left Wednesday's win at Indiana with a swollen right eye and a scratched left cornea. Houston did not say whether he will miss time before Friday at Denver, and Steven Adams opened the second half at center.
Alperen Sengun played on Friday, Nov. 20, despite a scratched cornea from Wednesday, and he wore goggles in the first quarter. He played 36 minutes, up from about 29 in his previous five games.
Sengun is questionable at Denver with an eye injury, and Clint Capela is out and Steven Adams is questionable, so Houston's center spot is the key late-slate decision.
Amen Thompson had 19 points, seven rebounds, four assists, and two blocks in 29 minutes. The show said it still wants more playing time for him, but the game was not close late.

Amen Thompson ran the point for Houston on November 15 with Fred VanVleet resting and Marcus Smart suspended, and he played 29 minutes with 26 points, seven rebounds and seven assists. The show said he is much more productive when he is the point guard, but his role has not been that this season. VanVleet returned on November 16.

Amen Thompson played 29 minutes in a 28-point win against WAS on Sunday, 6 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 49.2 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Thompson returned after missing one game with soreness, and that sent Tari Eason back to the bench. The show said Thompson looks much better than he did a couple of weeks ago, though sharing the ball with Fred VanVleet limits his ceiling.
Amen Thompson played only 26 minutes, his lowest total in recent games, and the show said his dip is real. The show was less willing to buy low on him than on Kevin Durant.

Andre Drummond has played 12 to 16 minutes off the bench in each of his last six games. The show said he can produce 30 fantasy points in 18 minutes but is only a large-field tournament dart, especially if Cup-game minutes tighten.

Andrew Nembhard returned from a hip injury on Friday, Nov. 20, after missing two games and went back into the starting lineup for 26 minutes. Braden Smith, who had started in his place, dropped to 11 minutes off the bench.

Nembhard is questionable at Cleveland with a hip sprain after missing two games; Rick Carlisle said it should not be a long absence. Quenton Jackson has started in his place with Tyrese Haliburton also out.
The show said Andrew Wiggins picked up most of Pelle Larsson's playing time on November 13, although he did not do much with it. Wiggins played 32 minutes off the bench and scored 8 points.

Andrew Wiggins has come off the bench since 11/08 after starting earlier in the month. The show said he has complained to the media about his role and that Pelle Larsson's absence could flip his minutes back up over time.

Andrew Wiggins played 34 minutes off the bench with Bam Adebayo leaving early and Pelle Larsson out, and he scored 17 points with three blocks. The show noted he took only nine shots and doubted he would do much more even if Adebayo misses time.
Anfernee Simons played just 15 minutes because of foul trouble and had 12 points with nothing else. The show said he is a hot-and-cold scorer who does not fit well on a good team.
Anfernee Simons moved into the starting lineup on Wednesday, Nov. 18, with Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown out, and he played 38 minutes.

Anthony Black had 20 points and 7 assists in 33 minutes against Boston on 11/16 in Jalen Suggs' first game back in the starting lineup. The show said it never expected Suggs' return to hurt Black much.

Anthony Black is carrying a big usage load while Paolo Banchero is out, but he had a rare off night with missed free throws and a poor shooting line on 16 shots. The show said Black's numbers should come down further when Banchero returns and his steals, blocks and free throw rate regress.

The show said Anthony Black's usage will go down when Paolo Banchero returns, which Orlando is targeting for about two weeks from now. The show said his role is already shifting as Jalen Suggs ramps up and Franz Wagner handles the ball more. Suggs has moved into the starting lineup, and Black scored 15 and 13 points in the two games after Suggs started playing over 30 minutes.

The show said Anthony Black got a big bump while Jalen Suggs was out and with Paolo Banchero still out, and that he needs around 30 minutes a night to keep producing. Black started every game Suggs missed from October 28 to November 11, and his minutes have stayed between 33 and 37 in the four games since Suggs returned. The show doubted he keeps that workload once Orlando is fully healthy, and Banchero has not played since October 23.
He missed Friday with his ankle sprain, and the show doubts he plays both games of the back-to-back that continues Saturday at Oklahoma City.

He has missed two straight games with his ankle sprain and is questionable again at Detroit. Kyshawn George scored 33 and 38.25 DK points in the two games without him, and the show expects George to be the most popular play if Davis sits.
Anthony Davis had 21 points and 13 rebounds in 34 minutes Wednesday, and Washington hosts Detroit on the second night of a back-to-back. The Wizards have not posted their injury report yet.

Anthony Davis has played legitimate starter minutes lately, with 35 and 34 minutes in his last two games and a 44-minute game on 11/12. The show said he is producing about 1.33 DraftKings points per minute and called his 11/20 matchup against a fast, poor Chicago defense the best spot among the top-salary players.
He is ruled out tonight.
He is ruled out tonight (arthroscopic procedure on his right knee).

Minnesota is again without Anthony Edwards, Donte DiVincenzo and Jaylen Clark against the Knicks, and Jonathan Kuminga is questionable with a right shoulder contusion. When Kuminga sat Tuesday, Trey Lyles played 31 minutes off the bench.
The show said Anthony Edwards had knee surgery and is out until sometime in January. He has not played in Minnesota's recent games.
Anthony Edwards is out again for Minnesota, along with Donte DiVincenzo and Jaylen Clark, so the Wolves lean on their bench wings and forwards against a short-handed Memphis team.
Asa Newell had surgery Tuesday to repair a plantar plate tear in his left big toe, hurt November 4. He will be re-evaluated in about four months.

Thompson played 43 minutes and posted his first triple-double on November 12, but he played only 18 minutes on November 14. The show said he has a very large role whenever games are competitive and he stays out of foul trouble.

Ausar Thompson has not made a three-pointer all season, but he averaged 3.3 steals and 1.7 blocks over his last three games through 11/17, and he added 12 assists in 29 minutes on 11/17. The show said he looks like he has finally been freed up after years of blood-clot problems and has a green light, though it called him a sell-high because a top-five pace will not last.

Austin Reaves is ruled out at Phoenix with a left heel bruise (X-rays negative, day-to-day). Collin Sexton is questionable after stitches over his eye, while Quentin Grimes is available with a splint on his finger.
He is ruled out tonight. Grimes is the main beneficiary and could post top-70 numbers in those games.
He is questionable tonight vs UTA.
Austin Reaves missed his fourth straight game on Friday, Nov. 20, with a bruised heel. The team has said there is nothing structural beyond the bone bruise.

Ayo Dosunmu has been Minnesota's starter with Anthony Edwards out, and Edwards has not played since 10/26 after a knee arthroscopy. Dosunmu played 39 minutes on 11/17 and has scored at least 24 points in four of his last six games. The show said the Edwards injury turned his season around and guessed he has about two more months in this role.

Dosunmu is starting and playing 30 to 39 minutes with Anthony Edwards out, but his scoring has swung wildly. He scored 8 points on 11/16, 30 points with seven threes on 11/17, and 6 points on 2-of-9 shooting on 11/19. The show called him a top-50 player and said Edwards' return will eventually cut into him, but not soon.
Dan Besbris listed Ayo Dosunmu as a top-50 season-long pickup because Anthony Edwards is out, which opens up minutes for him. Dosunmu played 32 minutes in his last game on 11/19.

The show said Bam Adebayo's usage rate is down about four points from last year while playing next to Giannis Antetokounmpo, and that his points and rebounds are lower. He is averaging about 2.2 steals per game through November 11, which the show called a likely mirage that will come back down.

The show said Bam Adebayo has rebuilt his game this season by mostly dropping his three-point attempts and working around the rim, which has pushed his field goal percentage to about 53 percent. It said his high steal rate is driving much of his fantasy value and could fall.

Bam Adebayo played 16 minutes in a 18-point win against HOU on Monday, 20 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 11 minutes of garbage time. His 11.8 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Bam Adebayo sat the second half Monday with right hip tightness; Miami called it proactive and does not think it is long-term. Giannis Antetokounmpo moved to center and Andrew Wiggins started the second half. Miami next plays Wednesday.

Scheierman started and played 29 minutes on 11/11 with Paul George out. The show said that game is why his recent rank looks good, since he played only 11 minutes in the next game and has stayed in a small bench role since George returned.

Baylor Scheierman played 18 minutes off the bench on November 15 and had 12 points and two steals. The show said Boston's bench minutes can go to Scheierman, Sam Hauser, Hugo Gonzalez or Jordan Walsh on any given night, which makes any of them hard to trust.

Baylor Scheierman scored 19.2 of his 27.2 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 37-point win against DAL on Sunday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.
Baylor Scheierman played only 11 minutes and scored zero points one game after a strong night, so the show admitted its call on him did not work.
Ben Sheppard is having surgery Wednesday to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee.
Ben Simmons is out for the season.
The show said Benedict Mathurin gets a bump with Dejounte Murray out while Murray waits to be traded. The show framed it as a deeper-league bump rather than a major role change.
Bennett Stirtz played 25 minutes off the bench on Friday, Nov. 20, as Oklahoma City rallied from 16 down, and he scored back-to-back baskets during the third-quarter comeback.
Bilal Coulibaly returned on Nov. 11 after missing Nov. 9 and played 25 minutes off the bench. The show said he is off the injury report and offers steals, blocks and a few assists.

Bobby Portis played 23 minutes after Bam Adebayo left with hip tightness, up from 14 to 20 minutes in his previous six games. The show said Portis is Miami's only other true center and should get at least 26 to 28 minutes if Adebayo sits, which has typically made him fantasy viable.

Bones Hyland has played 21 to 23 minutes in his last two games with Anthony Edwards out, up from 10 to 13 minutes earlier in the month. The show said Jaylen Clark's injury on November 14 and blowouts helped him, and it does not think his recent efficiency is sustainable.

The show said Bones Hyland should get 16 to 20 minutes off the bench while Anthony Edwards and Jaylen Clark are out. He played 23 and 21 minutes in his two games before Monday, but only 13 minutes on Monday night. The show said his strong recent numbers will not hold long term.

Hyland played 17 minutes on 11/17 and has played between 13 and 23 minutes in each of his last four games. The show said Minnesota keeps him around 15 to 16 minutes no matter who is in or out, which makes him riskier as his price rises to $4,500.
Smith has been in and out of the rotation, but he started the second half over Quenton Jackson on Wednesday and played 18 minutes. The show said it cannot trust him to play enough most nights.
Braden Smith went back to the bench on Friday, Nov. 20, when Andrew Nembhard returned, and he played only 11 minutes after starting four of the previous five games.
Bradley Beal (knee) has not played yet this season and is still recovering.

The show said Brandin Podziemski will be great with Stephen Curry out. Per the show, last season he averaged 17.5 points, 6.7 rebounds and 4.9 assists per 36 minutes with Curry off the floor, and this season's smaller sample is 18.2 points and 5.7 assists per 36. The show suggested taking about 10 percent off those rates as a fair expectation.

Brandin Podziemski is starting and playing about 30 minutes a night without Stephen Curry, but he scored only 10 points on Nov. 18. The show said it expected him to break out with Curry out and called his production a disappointment.

Golden State lost 126-98 at Memphis, which was its fourth straight blowout loss without Stephen Curry, who is out with a right oblique tear. The show said Brandin Podziemski is showing how hard it is to play without the open looks Curry creates for him.

Brandon Ingram (heel surgery) and Bradley Beal are out again for the Clippers. Darius Garland is playing through a back issue, and Keaton Wagler has played 25 to 28 minutes off the bench in each of his last three games.
The show said Brandon Ingram might be back for the Clippers' next game. His return would cut into minutes for wings like Kris Dunn, Derrick Jones Jr. and Keaton Wagler.
He is ruled out tonight (right heel surgery). Wagler becomes the second scoring option behind Garland.

The show said Brandon Ingram will not play Saturday but is set to return Monday, November 23, from his right heel surgery. It expects him to be frustrating early with minutes limits and back-to-back management.

He is out Monday with a hip strain, Kon Knueppel is out at least four more weeks and Dennis Schroder is out at least two weeks. Moussa Diabate is questionable, and the show named Hannes Steinbach as the fill-in if he sits.

Brandon Miller, Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder are all out at Phoenix, while Moussa Diabate and Grant Williams are probable. Sion James and Grayson Allen started Monday, and Allen scored 27 points with six threes.
Brandon Miller is off the injury report after missing two games with a hip strain, with Kon Knueppel and Dennis Schroder still out with hamstring strains.

Brandon Miller missed two games with a hip strain and came back on 11/15 with 5 points in 24 minutes at the Clippers. He moved up to 32 minutes and 28 points at the Lakers on 11/17 as his workload grew. The show said his shooting has been among the worst in the league but expects a hot scoring run to come.

Brandon Miller rolled his ankle on 11/20 against Atlanta but came back and finished with 33 minutes. The show said ankle sprains can flare up 24 to 48 hours later, so he should be watched on the next injury report.

Brandon Williams has a mild left hamstring strain and is out at least a week. Golden State is also without Jimmy Butler III, Kristaps Porzingis, Moses Moody and Gary Payton II at Houston, which is missing Clint Capela and Steven Adams.

The Warriors announced that Brandon Williams has returned to on-court activity and will be re-evaluated on Saturday, 11/21, so he is out at least until then. The show said his return would cut into LJ Cryer's role as the backup point guard, and Cryer has started on 11/16 and 11/18 while Williams has been out.
Brayden Burries has kept starting for Milwaukee, but his minutes have ranged from 19 to 29. The show said his role depends on whether he plays well enough for the team to keep him on the floor.

Brayden Burries started and played 29 minutes on November 15 in a game where starters Tyler Herro, Myles Turner and Kyle Kuzma played 20 to 23 minutes. The show said his minutes go up in blowouts while the veterans' minutes go down, which gives him a relatively safe floor.

Brayden Burries scored 20 points on nine shots in 25 minutes and has started the last nine games. He has reached 30 minutes only once in that stretch, and the show said Taylor Jenkins will not play guys 33 minutes, which limits his value.

Brayden Burries has been starting for the Bucks and playing roughly 23 to 29 minutes a night, with strong rebounding for a guard. The show said the struggling Bucks should hand more of the offense to their recent lottery pick as the season goes along, which could expand his role.

Sensabaugh's minutes climbed in every game from 11/6 to 11/17 (10, 13, 14, 23, 27, 30, 35), and he scored 40 points with eight threes off the bench in 35 minutes on 11/17. The show tied the jump to Lauri Markkanen being out of the lineup (Markkanen has not played since 11/6) and said Sensabaugh is filling that scoring gap. The box score shows his minutes fell back to 14 on 11/18 when Jaxson Hayes returned, so the trend is not locked in.

Sensabaugh's bench minutes are unstable. He played 35 minutes and scored 40 points with eight threes on 11/17, then played only 14 minutes on 11/18 and 26 minutes on 11/20. The show did not know why he was cut to 14 minutes and guessed it was a defensive benching. It said he gets buried when Utah is at full strength.

Brice Sensabaugh played the whole fourth quarter Tuesday and scored 25 of his 40 points in it as Utah pulled away from the Clippers. His bench minutes have climbed four straight games with Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. out, but Utah has not posted its report for tonight's back-to-back at the Lakers.
Brice Sensabaugh played 26 minutes off the bench on 11/20. The show said he has been playing well lately and is mainly a source of points and threes.

Brook Lopez has started at center ahead of Isaiah Jackson in every game since at least November 8, and he scored 26 points on November 13. The show said the switch to the starting lineup sparked his run, but it expects the frontcourt to get crowded when Yanic Konan Niederhauser returns from foot surgery.

Brook Lopez played 29 minutes on November 15 and had eight assists even though he shot poorly. The show said he was the only Clippers starter who held up in that game, finishing plus two. The show called him the clearest hold among the Clippers starters.

The show said Lopez has been humming along since he moved into the Clippers' starting lineup, and he has started every game since Nov. 2. It said he is top 50 in fantasy over the last week but worried that the fun may not last on a losing team.

Brook Lopez played 23 minutes in a 25-point loss against UTA on Tuesday, 5 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 5 minutes of garbage time. His 39.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.

Brook Lopez has started at center for the Clippers and scored 23 points in each of his last two games while Isaiah Jackson's bench minutes shrank to nine on November 19. The show said Lopez is playing well and that the backup center spot is unsettled.

Buddy Hield played 25 minutes off the bench on November 13 and stayed on the floor late while playing well. The show said Chicago will need bench production without Caleb Wilson and called him a stream option on light days.

Buddy Hield had been out of Chicago's rotation behind Jordan Hawkins, but he played 25 and 20 minutes on November 13 and 14 after Caleb Wilson went down. The show said his usage is up, but it does not trust his three-point shooting to hold.

The show said Cade Cunningham carries about a 30% usage rate and a 38% assist rate this season with about 56.5% true shooting. It projected him at about 51 DK points on 11/12 and called him the best stud play on the slate even though Washington plays at a slow pace.
Jalen Duren (hamstring) and Isaiah Joe (hip) are both ruled out at Miami. Cade Cunningham played 48 minutes Thursday and scored 52 points, and Paul Reed played 38 minutes at center.

Cade Cunningham returned on 11/20 after he missed the Pistons' 11/18 game and played 36 minutes. The show said there was never much concern about the knee and that the missed game was more of a night off.

Martin started and played 33 and 34 minutes on 11/14 and 11/15 while Max Christie did not play. The show asked whether his minutes bump was tied to blowouts or to Christie's absence and was not interested. Christie returned on 11/18 for 8 minutes, and Martin played 20 minutes as a starter.

Martin has started every game since 11/6, and his minutes went up to 33 and 34 on 11/14 and 11/15 before he played 20 on 11/18. The show said his minutes and starts have been rising, but it is worried about his knee. It also noted that Dallas plays on both Saturday and Sunday.

Caleb Martin played 20 minutes in a 22-point win against GSW on Wednesday, 5 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 21.2 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.
Caleb Wilson missed his fifth straight game on Friday, Nov. 20, after surgery on his right hand on Nov. 12.
Cam Johnson was out on Oct. 28 and is expected to return fairly soon.
Ty Jerome and Scotty Pippen Jr. are both questionable Saturday against Sacramento. Spencer has moved ahead of Pippen in the rotation and had eight assists in 23 minutes Thursday.

With Ty Jerome out again with a hip injury (Jerome has not played since 11/13), Spencer has started and played 34 and 32 minutes on 11/14 and 11/16. He had nine assists on 11/16. The show called him the main guard while Jerome is out and a start in standard leagues.

Cam Spencer should start again Wednesday because Ty Jerome is out. In the two games Jerome missed, Spencer started and played 34 and 32 minutes for 34.3 and 33.0 DraftKings points. Off the bench before that, he played 17 to 24 minutes.

Cam Spencer has been starting for Memphis while Ty Jerome is out with a hip injury, and he scored 26 points with five threes in 29 minutes on Nov. 18. The show said there is still no clear timeline for Jerome, who has not played since Nov. 13, so Spencer's lead guard role could last anywhere from days to a month.

Cam Spencer has started every game since Ty Jerome got hurt after November 13, playing 27 to 34 minutes as a starter. He averaged about 18 points and eight assists over the three starts before November 19, then posted 11 assists in 27 minutes on November 19 with Jerome out again. The show said Spencer should be held even after Jerome returns to see how the roles shake out.
Dan Besbris listed Cam Spencer as a top-75 season-long pickup because Ty Jerome is out, which opens up minutes for him. Spencer played 27 minutes in his last game on 11/19.

Cameron Boozer made seven threes and scored 29 points on 11/16, but he played only 29 minutes because Memphis was comfortably ahead. The show said he normally settles into a 32 to 33 minute role and liked him against Cleveland with Evan Mobley out and Ty Jerome out on his own side.

With Ty Jerome out on Monday, Cameron Boozer took on more of the scoring and set a season high with 29 points, making 7 of 13 threes, including two during the 10-0 third-quarter run that tied the game.
Boozer has played 29, 29 and 28 minutes in his last three games, including competitive ones. The show said the minutes cap is frustrating but that he still has a strong ceiling and floor at $8,400.

Memphis is short again at Cleveland: Ty Jerome (right hip) and Isaiah Stewart (illness) are out, and GG Jackson had foot surgery Tuesday and will be re-evaluated in about three months. Boozer, Cam Spencer and Jerami Grant carry more of the load.
Boozer had 18 points, eight rebounds, five assists and four steals on Wednesday, and he led Memphis in DraftKings points. The show said he is cooking right now.

The show said Cameron Boozer's playmaking has taken a step forward and that he looks comfortable in Memphis's system. He has started all 16 games, averaging about 31 minutes with roughly nine rebounds and five assists per game. The show called him a triple-double threat, though his only double-digit assist game so far came on October 29.
He is ruled out tonight (right ankle sprain).
Cameron Carr made his debut Sunday and played 1 minute late in the game without scoring.
Cameron Johnson picked up five fouls and still played 27 minutes, but he had nine points and no rebounds. The show said to move on from him.
Cameron Johnson had one of his better games with 19 points on 13 shots. The show said it was no surprise that it came on a night when Jamal Murray shot poorly and someone else had to score.
LeVert played for the first time this season on Wednesday and scored eight points in eight minutes. He is another name in a crowded Milwaukee guard rotation.
Caris LeVert played the final 11 minutes of the November 19 game and was in Milwaukee's closing lineup. The show could not explain the choice, which adds to the Bucks' rotation chaos.

Carter Bryant played 13 minutes on November 19 with Dylan Harper out, after 2 and 5 minutes in the two games before. The show said he was the Spurs' first player off the bench in that game, which gives him more minutes upside.
The show said Wallace is presumably out for the season. He has not played since Oct. 25.
Cedric Coward played 33 minutes and scored 54.5 DraftKings points on 11/14 with Ty Jerome out. The show said he has been incredible lately, although it wished his 6,500 salary was a little lower.

The show said Cedric Coward's minutes swing from game to game, but his rebounding has been consistently strong, partly because Zach Edey has been off the floor so much. Over his last 11 games before November 16, the box scores show 14.4 points, 9.0 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game.

The show said Cedric Coward has been excellent without Ty Jerome. He has scored 41 or more DraftKings points in each of the two games Jerome missed (11/14 and 11/16). The show also liked his rebound numbers against a Cleveland team missing Evan Mobley and possibly Peyton Watson.

The show said Cedric Coward has been very productive for fantasy even on relatively low usage. He had 18 points, 8 rebounds and 6 assists in 27 minutes on only 10 shots, and the show doubted the rebounding pace will hold all season.

Cedric Coward played 25 minutes in a 28-point win against GSW on Thursday, 5 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 11 minutes of garbage time. His 36.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.
The show said Cedric Coward's breakout season continues and it is not sure it is cooling off. He had 19 points with five threes on November 19 and has scored 18 or more in four straight games.

Chaney Johnson scored 10.0 of his 10.0 DraftKings points in garbage time of a 30-point loss against CHI on Wednesday, when the lead was 20 or more late. His line is bigger than his normal role; expect less in a close game.

The show said Al Horford and Draymond Green were questionable for 11/18 and that Bassey is a cheap DFS play if they sit. Horford did not play on 11/18, and Bassey started and had 10 points and eight rebounds in 22 minutes. The show said he blocks shots but gives no steals or threes, and that it would fade him if Horford and Green both play.

Bassey has started two straight games, with Al Horford out on 11/18 and Draymond Green out on 11/19. He played 22 and 25 minutes in those starts and posted 16 points and 13 rebounds on 11/19. The show said Horford can no longer handle big minutes and Golden State is leaning on Bassey, and the open question is whether he can hold 25-plus minutes and stay healthy.

Chaz Lanier played 25 minutes on Tuesday only because Detroit was missing Ronald Holland II and Duncan Robinson, and he scored just 3 points. The show said his minutes should mostly disappear as injured players return.
He is out 8 to 10 weeks with a small patellar tendon tear, so Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara take on the frontcourt minutes.
He is ruled out tonight. Mara had 11 points, 10 rebounds and two blocks in 20 minutes Monday with Holmgren out.
Holmgren remained out Wednesday against Atlanta. Isaiah Hartenstein grabbed 17 rebounds in his place.

Chris Cenac Jr. jumped into the rotation for 12 minutes with Neemias Queta resting. The show said he looked very athletic and that Joe Mazzulla talked him up after the game, so he is someone to keep in mind.

Chris Cenac Jr.'s minutes have climbed from 7 to 12 to 17 over the Celtics' last three games. The show said Joe Mazzulla could try big lineups with Cenac starting next to Paul George and Jayson Tatum, because Jordan Walsh played only 4 minutes after starting on November 18 and Baylor Scheierman's minutes have fallen to around 10 to 18.
The show thinks Chris Youngblood will be out a while longer. He has a right heel contusion and has not played in Portland's recent games.

Christian Anderson had his best game as a pro with 16 points, four threes and two steals while Dennis Schroder was out with a hamstring strain. The show said it hopes Charlotte keeps him in that role after Schroder returns.

The show said Anderson is finally playing well, but his minutes are limited and should shrink further as Charlotte gets healthier. He has played 16 to 18 minutes in each of his last three games off the bench.

Christian Braun started and played 28 minutes against New Orleans, and he was Denver's third-best DraftKings scorer behind Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray for the third time in the last six games. The show said Braun is the third Nugget with value more often than not, but it doubted that holds all season.

CJ McCollum played 32 minutes on November 13 after playing 21 to 25 minutes in four of his previous five games. Kingston Flemings left that game with a back injury after 17 scoreless minutes. The show said the question is whether McCollum moves from a 24-minute role to about 27 minutes while Flemings is struggling or unavailable.

CJ McCollum played 32 minutes off the bench at Chicago after Kingston Flemings left early, scoring 20 points with 5 rebounds and 5 assists. The show said he has been a high-usage bench player for a few games and will play more in the short term.

CJ McCollum moved back into Atlanta's starting lineup on November 15 with Kingston Flemings out with a lumbar back issue, and he played 30 minutes. He scored 20 points with four steals, and the show said he went nine for nine at the free-throw line. The show treated Flemings as day-to-day.
CJ McCollum missed his second straight game on Friday, Nov. 20, with a left calf strain. He is set to be re-evaluated in about four weeks.
Capela started on Oct. 30 with Alperen Sengun and Steven Adams out, but he is now out himself. He missed Nov. 2 with a right ankle sprain.
The show said Charlotte plays only five games over the next 14 days, which is a very light schedule. This limits how many DFS slates the Hornets appear on during that stretch.

White played 16, 18 and 16 minutes in his first three games and then 20 minutes in each of his next three. He scored 21 points on November 15 even with Brandon Miller and Naz Reid playing. The show said it is waiting for his minutes to rise to around 24 before trusting him at $5,400.

White played 26 minutes on 11/17 after being held to 20 minutes in each of his previous two games. The show said Charlotte has been careful with White and Brandon Miller because of their injury histories, and it expects White to have a big role going forward.

Charlotte has ramped up Coby White's minutes slowly since his return, from 16, 18 and 16 minutes in his first three games to 20 minutes in three straight and then 26 minutes on 11/17. He scored 21, 21 and 19 points in those last three games despite the cap. The show said his usage is through the roof and that he is starting to look like himself again.

Coby White has played 26 minutes in each of his last two games after he sat at 20 minutes in the two games before that. The show said he is slowly working back toward his full role and looked good even though his shot was not falling.

Cody Williams started for Minnesota on 11/17 and played 13 minutes after logging between 2 and 7 minutes off the bench in his earlier games. The show said he becomes interesting in deep leagues only if Minnesota keeps starting him.
Cody Williams started on November 17 while Jonathan Kuminga was out, but he did not play at all on November 19 once Kuminga returned. He has no role when Minnesota's forwards are healthy.

Collin Gillespie outplayed Jalen Green and got more minutes than him on November 12, playing 27 minutes off the bench. The show said his bench role makes him harder to trust, but the minutes are trending in his favor.

Collin Gillespie played 27 minutes off the bench against Charlotte and scored 13 points. The show said this was a high-water mark and that he got a few extra minutes because the reserves won the game while Jalen Green played poorly. Jordan Goodwin also got extra minutes and played 24.

Collin Gillespie's minutes are rising off the bench, with 28 on 11/15 and 27 on 11/12 after 20-24 in the three games before. The show said Phoenix needs a true point guard and is starting to recognize that playing him more helps.

Collin Gillespie played 26 minutes off the bench and has played 26 to 28 minutes in each of his last three games. The show said Phoenix looks bad without a true point guard and Gillespie is the only one on the roster, so it expects his minutes to stay at 25 or more unless the Suns trade for a guard.

Collin Gillespie played only 17 minutes in a blowout of Sacramento after playing 26 to 28 minutes in recent games. The show said his role depends on whether Phoenix needs a point guard in a given game, so he is hard to trust.
Collin Murray-Boyles returned on Nov. 11 and started, playing 20 minutes after missing Nov. 9. The show expects him to be available Thursday.

Collin Murray-Boyles stayed in Toronto's starting lineup at center when Scottie Barnes returned on November 15, and he played 40 minutes in an overtime game. The show said this answers the question of who starts at center once Barnes plays power forward. The show warned that Toronto's back-to-back on Tuesday and Wednesday could muddy the next data point.
Collin Murray-Boyles started at center over Jakob Poeltl on Sunday and played 40 minutes, including all of overtime, while Scottie Barnes returned from a four-game groin absence with 36 minutes.

Murray-Boyles started at center again on Nov. 17 and played 33 minutes, which the show called the number that matters most. The show said Toronto has made a straight-up benching of Jakob Poeltl whenever Murray-Boyles and Scottie Barnes are both active. On Nov. 18 he started again but played only 5 minutes, and the show gave no reason because it aired before that game.

Collin Murray-Boyles started and played 33 minutes against the Knicks, which the show said is the workload it wanted to see. He grabbed only one rebound, but he added three blocks and a steal. The show said he is in great shape with Jakob Poeltl moving to the bench.

Collin Murray-Boyles missed the 11/20 game while in the concussion protocol after playing only five minutes on 11/18. The show said there is no clear timeline, since he could miss one game or a full week depending on when his symptoms clear.

Sexton has averaged 14.2 points over his last five games through Nov. 17 while coming off the bench, and the show tied the bump to Austin Reaves being out. His minutes have stayed in the 20 to 27 range in that stretch. His role should shrink once Reaves returns.
Collin Sexton played 18 minutes off the bench on 11/20. The show said he is only a streaming option on a favorable slate.

Cooper Flagg played 27 minutes in a 37-point loss against BOS on Sunday, 6 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 30.2 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.
The show said the Dallas coach told the media that Cooper Flagg gets lazy on defense when his shots are not falling. The show liked Flagg under $10,000 and hoped the comment fires him up.
Dallas is without Dereck Lively II, and P.J. Washington and Walter Clayton Jr. are questionable. The Clippers are missing Bradley Beal and Brandon Ingram.

Corey Kispert played 16 minutes off the bench on November 15 while Luguentz Dort played 18 and Aaron Wiggins played 24. The show said the wing minutes will keep rotating among Dort, Wiggins and Kispert and that Dorian Finney-Smith has not really been in the rotation.

Craig Porter Jr. played 28 minutes off the bench on November 14 while Cleveland's regular starters sat. The show called him a very good producer when he gets minutes, but it said Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor are both ahead of him in the rotation right now.
The show said Oklahoma City waived Dalen Terry a few days after signing him, as part of the move to get Nique Clifford. Terry played five and six minutes in his two games with the Thunder.
He played 37 minutes Friday, and the show labeled him and Robert Williams III doubtful for Saturday against San Antonio on the back-to-back.

Damian Lillard has started all 10 of his games and averages about 29 minutes and 20 points in the box scores. The show said blowouts have cut his minutes, with his scoring near 22 points in competitive games and much lower in lopsided ones. He played just 20 minutes on Nov 7 and 24 minutes on Nov 10.
Lillard played both games of the back-to-back against the Thunder, scoring 18 points in 32 minutes on the second night. The show said his usage is not as high as expected.

The show called November 13 a big usage game for Damian Lillard, who took 18 shots and 11 free throws in 33 minutes with Ja Morant out. The show said his free throw percentage is climbing toward 90 percent.
Damian Lillard played 31 minutes on the second night of the back-to-back Tuesday, up from 24 Monday, when Portland emptied its bench late.

With Deni Avdija out on 11/17, Lillard took 19 shots in 31 minutes and scored 25 points. The show said he had a team-leading 33.5% usage rate without Avdija and that Portland may have held his minutes down because it was the second leg of a back-to-back.

Portland plays Minnesota again on the second night of a back-to-back, and the Blazers had not posted their injury report Tuesday morning. Lillard played only 24 minutes Monday after Portland emptied its bench down 19 late.
Lillard played 35 minutes Thursday at Milwaukee with Deni Avdija (left foot) and Ja Morant (hamstring) out, and he scored a season-high 33 in his first game back in Milwaukee.

Daniel Gafford played 19 minutes as a starter on November 15 after suffering a stinger in his previous game. The show said he is still useful in about 21 minutes a night and needs only around 22 minutes to provide value, so it is not giving up on him.
Gafford started but had only six points and six rebounds in 24 minutes. The show said he has been outside the top 200 over the last two weeks and does not need to be held.

Daniel Gafford played 24 minutes as the starting center, his most since early November after several games in the 16 to 20 range. The show said 24 minutes long-term is enough for value, there is still no news on Dereck Lively II, and Morez Johnson Jr. only takes Gafford's minutes when Gafford leaves mid-game.

Daniss Jenkins moved into Detroit's starting lineup on 11/09 and has played 35 to 42 minutes in every game since, after coming off the bench for 21 to 24 minutes earlier in the season. The show said Cade Cunningham talked after the 11/17 win over San Antonio about how important Jenkins' play was to the win, and the show believes his role is sustainable.

Detroit came back from 14 down to end San Antonio's 12-game winning streak with Kevin Huerter starting for Duncan Robinson and Ausar Thompson running more offense. Detroit plays at New Orleans on the second night of a back-to-back and has not posted its injury report.
Daniss Jenkins started and played 39 minutes on 11/20 even with Cade Cunningham back in the lineup. The show said he has less to do with Cunningham back but remains a must-roster player.

Danny Wolf went back to the bench on 11/16 and played only 11 minutes after starting four straight games with 28 to 36 minutes. The show said Brooklyn's coach seems to pick night to night who plays, rotating among Wolf, Nolan Traore, Keon Ellis and Noah Clowney.
Wolf has lost the starting job he held earlier, coming off the bench on 11/16 and 11/18 after starting on 11/11 and 11/14. The show said his 30-minute starting role is over.
Danny Wolf started in place of Egor Demin on Friday, Nov. 20, and played 26 minutes.

Darius Acuff Jr. took 25 shots for 26 points on November 15 and committed nine turnovers. The show said coach Doug Christie has given him a license to shoot freely as part of his development and suggested this is frustrating Domantas Sabonis.

The show said Sacramento is simply giving Darius Acuff Jr. the ball, and that even Zach LaVine has embraced handing him the keys. Acuff has started and played 33 to 40 minutes in recent games, including 36 points in 35 minutes on November 18, though the show noted he rarely shoots over 50 percent.

The show said Darius Acuff Jr. has a complete green light and that his usage and minutes will be through the roof all season. He has started all 15 games, averaging about 37 minutes and nearly 23 shot attempts per game. The show warned his efficiency can hurt some nights, but the volume is what drives his value.
The show said there is a risk the Clippers limit his playing time later in the season if the team keeps losing and has injuries.

Garland played 35 to 37 minutes in each of his last two games and scored at least 41 DraftKings points in three of his last four. The show said his minutes and production have risen as the Clippers have played more competitive games and won more often.

Darius Garland scored 27 points with seven assists while Brandon Ingram remained out after heel surgery. The show said it would like more usage from him during Ingram's absence and that his turnovers have been high.

The show said no Clipper plays big minutes, with Darius Garland the leader at 33 minutes per game and Rui Hachimura next at 29. The box scores match, with Garland at 33.2 and Hachimura at 29.0 minutes per game. The show said this makes a large minutes load for a returning Brandon Ingram unlikely.

Garland has played 35 and 37 minutes as a starter in his last two games. The show also liked Keaton Wagler as a sneaky value after he played 28 minutes off the bench on Nov. 15.

Darius Garland has played 35, 30 and 35 minutes in his last three games with Brandon Ingram out, and he scored 23 points on November 19. The show said Garland is finally playing more like it expected and hopes the run lasts more than three games.

Darius Garland played 35 minutes and took a team-high 17 shots while committing only one turnover. The show said his high turnovers have been the main problem this season and that his steals should climb back toward normal. The show also worried that the losing Clippers could give him rest days.

Darryn Peterson has played 33 or 34 minutes in each of Utah's last three games as a starter while Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. are out. The show said it really likes both Peterson and Keyonte George on Nov. 17 and expects George to play in the low 30s in minutes.
Peterson played only 19 minutes because he picked up four fouls, after playing at least 31 minutes in each of his previous four games. The show said he is in a funk but it is not too worried.

The show said injuries on Utah have opened up more usage and more minutes for Darryn Peterson. He has started all 17 games and has played 31 to 35 minutes in most recent games. The show added that rookie guards usually improve over the second half of the season.

Davion Mitchell has been Miami's starting point guard and has scored 41 or more DraftKings points in three straight games, including 16 points, 10 assists and 4 steals against Houston on 11/16. The show said he does it every night and is still priced at $7,000.

Mitchell scored 24 points with six assists and six threes in 36 minutes. The show said his minutes, usage and responsibility have been far beyond what it expected, and it does not see him as a sell-high, though his shooting is well above his expected points.

The show said Davion Mitchell has become a high-minute lead ball handler next to Giannis Antetokounmpo instead of being pushed aside, and it called him the favorite for Most Improved Player. He has played 32 to 39 minutes in each of his last five games with six to 17 assists. The show expects his three-point percentage to come down but thinks the minutes and assist role can hold.

The show said Davion Mitchell has settled in as the secondary scorer and lead facilitator behind Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo on a thin Miami roster. He has started all 15 games and averaged about 35 minutes with roughly nine assists per game. The show said Erik Spoelstra clearly trusts him and that his minutes and usage look locked in.

Day'Ron Sharpe played only 25 minutes on 11/16 because of foul trouble. The show said not to worry about it and that Sharpe has settled into a steady role alongside Julius Randle and Michael Porter Jr.
Day'Ron Sharpe started and played 26 minutes on 11/20. The show said no one is threatening his minutes, though the assist numbers he posted early in the season have tapered off.

De'Aaron Fox (left hip soreness) and Devin Vassell are questionable for San Antonio against Golden State, and Tobias Harris is out. Dylan Harper had 18 points and 10 assists in 36 minutes Wednesday and would handle more of the offense if Fox sits.
De'Aaron Fox returned to the starting lineup Tuesday after missing Sunday's game and played 34 minutes, and he was on the floor to close the game.

The show said Fox has been the fourth option in San Antonio's usage behind Wembanyama, Harper and Castle. With Harper's groin injury, the show expected Fox and Castle to gain the most. It noted that when Fox himself missed a game, the streamers did not gain much because his usage is not that high.
De'Aaron Fox missed Sunday's game but is not on San Antonio's injury report tonight. Tobias Harris (calf) is likely out until early December.
De'Aaron Fox did not take on more work in the first game without Dylan Harper, taking only five shots in 32 minutes. The show said this was odd but not a long-term worry.

The show said Fox has been on the injury report for most of the season with minor issues and wondered if San Antonio is managing him early. He still played 32 minutes on 11/19, so this is a risk to watch rather than an absence.

De'Andre Hunter played 37 minutes on 11/20 as every Kings starter played at least 36 minutes. The show said Sacramento is pumping a lot of minutes into Hunter and is running a top-heavy rotation that is easy to project.

The show listed De'Andre Hunter as questionable for Saturday. He played 37 minutes and scored 30 points on November 20, and the Kings are on the second night of a back-to-back, so the show said a rest is possible.

De'Anthony Melton came off the bench for 21 minutes on 11/16 while LJ Cryer started, after Melton had started the game before. The show said the last two games without Stephen Curry were blowouts and that Melton played 27 to 28 minutes in competitive games Curry missed earlier, on 10/24 and 11/1, so it expects more minutes in a close game such as the next one against Dallas.

De'Anthony Melton has played 18, 21 and 19 minutes in the three games without Stephen Curry because the games were lopsided early. The show said 27 or more minutes would make him a must-roster player and gave him one more chance in a competitive game at Memphis.

De'Anthony Melton started and played 25 minutes, his most since November 11, with Stephen Curry still out. The show said 25 minutes puts him inside the top 100 in fantasy and 27 minutes could push him toward the top 80, mostly from threes and steals. The show noted the Warriors had previously kept him near 19 minutes in blowout losses.
Dan Besbris listed De'Anthony Melton as a player he is still assessing because Stephen Curry is out, which opens up minutes for him. Melton played 25 minutes in his last game on 11/19.

Dean Wade started every game this season that LeBron James or Joel Embiid missed, playing 28 minutes on Oct. 24, 37 minutes on Oct. 25 and 30 minutes on Oct. 31, while coming off the bench at about 18 to 23 minutes otherwise. The show said Wade probably starts and plays 30-plus minutes if LeBron or Embiid sits and could get 90-plus minutes over Philadelphia's next three games.

Dean Wade played 35 minutes off the bench on November 15 with Joel Embiid out. The show said everyone else on Philadelphia got more usage without Embiid but Wade did not, and that he does not reach fantasy value no matter how many minutes he plays.
Dean Wade played 35 minutes off the bench with Joel Embiid out, but he took only 5 shots. The show said his ultra-low usage makes sustained value almost impossible even when the minutes are there.

Wade started with LeBron James out and played 32 minutes with 11 rebounds. The show said Wade is generally the next man up when James sits. It also said he is a much better real-life player than a fantasy player.

Dean Wade has played 32 to 35 minutes in his last three games and should keep a big role with Jaylen Brown out Wednesday. His DraftKings output swings hard, though: 16.3 points in 34 minutes on November 12 and 29.8 in 32 minutes on Monday. He scores little himself, so he needs rebounds and threes to hit value.
Wade sat Wednesday at Orlando with a hamstring issue.
DeAndre Jordan started at center for New Orleans on November 13 and played 17 minutes. The show said he started for no clear reason and should not be added.
DeAndre Jordan started at center on November 13 but did not play on November 14 once Yves Missi returned to the starting lineup. The show said Jordan is now out of the rotation.

The show said the Pelicans are trying to trade Dejounte Murray and want to give Jeremiah Fears as many touches as he can handle. Murray has cooled off with 7, 6, and 12 points in his last three games, and he played only 18 minutes on Nov 9. The show said his steals keep his value steady even with a usage rate around 20 percent.

Dejounte Murray started and played 28 minutes but had only five points and four assists. The show said he is barely getting the ball and is outside the top 140 over the last two weeks despite heavy minutes.
Dejounte Murray has not played since November 11 and missed the Pelicans' games on November 13 and 14. The show said his trade request is the reason he is not playing.

Dejounte Murray has not played since 11/11, and the show said New Orleans shut him down about four days ago amid trade talk. The show cited reports that teams expect the Pelicans to attach draft assets in a deal, and it noted the Suns were linked but have denied interest. The show guessed he could be out about a month.
Dejounte Murray remains away from the team. The show cited Jake Fischer reporting that Murray views Phoenix as an attractive landing spot and that Phoenix wants a more viable big man.

Dejounte Murray was ruled out on November 20 with a left ankle sprain and has missed five straight games. The show said it believes he will never play another game for the Pelicans and may be hard to trade. That is the show's opinion, and the official reason for his absence is the ankle sprain.
DeMar DeRozan played 22 minutes off the bench on 11/20 after he played 25 minutes on 11/18. The show said it is good to see him getting more involved over his last couple of games.

The show said Deni Avdija's efficiency and assists have been solid with Ja Morant out, but it wants to see how his usage shifts when Morant returns. Avdija scored 34 points in 35 minutes on November 13, and Morant is out at least four weeks with a left hamstring strain.
Deni Avdija scored 27 points and is ranked 21st over the last two weeks. The show said Ja Morant's absence and Shaedon Sharpe being out funnel more usage to him.
Portland lists Deni Avdija and Toumani Camara (abdominal soreness) as questionable at Milwaukee, with Ja Morant, Shaedon Sharpe, Vit Krejci and Robert Williams III (rest) out.
Deni Avdija missed the Tuesday and Thursday games with a left foot injury, his first absences of the season, and Jayson Kent started both games. He is questionable for Saturday, Nov. 21, at New York.

Deni Avdija is questionable with a left foot contusion after missing two straight games, and Portland is still without Ja Morant, Shaedon Sharpe and Vit Krejci. Jayson Kent started both games Avdija missed.
He is ruled out tonight (left hamstring strain).
Dereck Lively II remains out with a broken foot. The show said it had seen nothing suggesting he is close to returning.

The show said Derik Queen has not been able to get consistent minutes even with Yves Missi out and Karlo Matkovic as the main obstacle, and that Missi's return makes his path harder. Queen has come off the bench in every game, ranging from 10 to 29 minutes. In Missi's first game back on November 14, Queen still played 25 minutes off the bench while Matkovic fell to 14.

Derik Queen had 17 points and 10 rebounds in only 21 minutes off the bench because Yves Missi is the starter and the team prefers it that way. The show called Queen a player who needs big efficiency in limited time to pay off.
Queen played 19 minutes off the bench and has not started. The show thinks both Zion Williamson and Yves Missi would probably need to be out before Queen starts.
Derik Queen played 18 minutes off the bench on 11/20, which continues a slide from 23 and 25 minutes earlier in the month. The show said the minutes will be a source of frustration for him.
The show named Derrick Jones Jr. its dud of the night after eight points and two rebounds in 27 minutes. The show guessed he is the starter most likely to go to the bench when Brandon Ingram returns.
The show expects Derrick Jones Jr. to be the starter who goes to the bench when Brandon Ingram returns on Monday. Jones played 27 minutes as a starter on November 19 while Max Strus also started.

Derrick White played 23 minutes in a 37-point win against DAL on Sunday, 7 under his average over his previous 5 games, and sat most of the 12 minutes of garbage time. His 30.0 DraftKings points likely undersell his normal role.
The show said every opponent Orlando has faced so far ranks 13th or better in defensive rating, including Boston, Toronto twice, New York, Minnesota and Washington.
The show said Desmond Bane's usage will drop once Paolo Banchero returns, but not by much. With Banchero out, Bane played 35 minutes and scored 21 points with six three-pointers on November 13.
The show said Jalen Suggs's return will make it harder for Bane to pay off his price consistently. Bane scored 15 points in 38 minutes on 11/18 in Suggs's second game back.
Phoenix hosts the Clippers on the second night of a back-to-back after a 26-point loss to San Antonio, where Booker scored 32 in 29 minutes. Phoenix has not posted its injury report yet.

Devin Booker played only 28 minutes in an eight-point game on November 15 because Phoenix's starters were badly outscored and the bench played more. Collin Gillespie, Luke Kennard and Jordan Goodwin all got big bench roles in that game. The show said to throw this game out, because the starters will normally be the players who get the minutes.
Devin Booker sat the whole fourth quarter Sunday as Collin Gillespie led a bench rally from 31 down against the Lakers. Phoenix plays at Denver tonight on the second night of a back-to-back.

Phoenix again spread its minutes almost evenly, with Jordan Goodwin (28) and Collin Gillespie (27) off the bench playing more than starters Dillon Brooks, Miles Bridges and Jalen Green (25 each). Devin Booker was the only Sun above 28 minutes at 38, and the show said nobody else on the team clearly needs to be rostered.
The show said he is questionable at Phoenix, which would move Julian Champagnie into a bigger role after he has played about 21 to 22 minutes a game off the bench.

The show said Vassell is a little more well-rounded than Champagnie but a worse shooter, and that he becomes rosterable while Harper is out. It said his 1.6 steals per game will not hold. He started and played 36 minutes on Nov. 17.

Devin Vassell started and played 32 minutes in the first game without Dylan Harper. The show said Vassell becomes a play in all formats while Harper is out because Harper's usage is now available. The show expects Vassell to contribute steals and assists more than threes.
Dan Besbris listed Devin Vassell as a top-100 season-long pickup because Dylan Harper is out, which opens up minutes for him. Vassell played 32 minutes in his last game on 11/19.
Dillon Brooks played only 25 minutes on 11/20 because he fouled out. The show said the foul-out was no surprise.
The show said Domantas Sabonis has basically asked to be traded. He had 16 points and 17 rebounds in 35 minutes on Wednesday.

Domantas Sabonis took only two shots and scored zero points in 24 minutes on November 10. The show said he looked completely disinterested and believes it was a sign he wants out of Sacramento, unless a hidden injury explains it. He bounced back with 21 points and 12 rebounds in 35 minutes on November 13.

The show said the Plumlee signing is not tied to a Sabonis injury, according to James Ham. The show doubted a Sabonis trade or shutdown because of his roughly $45 million salary, and it called the Kings' center picture with Dylan Cardwell and Maxime Raynaud too unclear to chase.
The show said Domantas Sabonis is barely touching the ball with Darius Acuff Jr. running the offense. The show projected him for about 4.7 assists.

The show said Domantas Sabonis looked engaged and motivated on November 13, coming off a game in which he seemed to give up. He was very aggressive early and slowed a little late, finishing with 21 points and 12 rebounds in 35 minutes.
